QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_19

question.text: Ritu's NAV grew from Rs.15.00 to Rs.21.00 over 4 years. What is the CAGR?

explanation.text: The Logic: CAGR = ((End Value / Beginning Value)^(1/n)) - 1 = ((21/15)^(1/4)) - 1 = (1.40)^(0.25) - 1 = 1.0878 - 1 = 0.0878, or about 8.78%. The Trap: Option A (10.00%) is the simple-annualization result (40% / 4 years) and ignores compounding. Option C (40.00%) is the total cumulative return over 4 years, not the annualized rate. Option D (15.00%) does not follow from any standard return formula on these inputs. Note: Distributor coaching tone removed; explanation rewritten as a concise source-backed CAGR formula application.
